name: Cable Standing Reverse Grip Curl (Straight bar)
description: A loaded carry or hold that hammers the finger flexors and grip while the whole forearm braces. Performed with a cable.
instructions: Stand tall holding the handle at your sides with a firm, full grip and your shoulders back.
Brace your core, pull your shoulders down, and stand as tall as you can.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps, keeping the weight steady and your posture upright — or simply hold the position and grip hard if you're not walking.
Keep crushing your grip the whole time and breathe steadily.
Set the weight down under control when your grip is nearly spent. Never let it slip.

name: Barbell Reverse Curl
description: A palms-down curl that builds the brachioradialis and forearm extensors, adding width to the upper forearm. Performed with a barbell.
instructions: Stand tall and grip the bar with your palms facing down, hands about shoulder-width apart and arms straight.
Keep your upper arms pinned to your sides and your wrists firm and straight.
Curl the weight up by bending only at the elbows, leading with the backs of your hands.
Squeeze your forearms and brachioradialis at the top.
Lower the bar slowly all the way down under control and repeat. Don't swing — keep the upper arms still.

name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
description: A reverse wrist-curl that targets the forearm extensors on top of the forearm for balanced, healthy wrists. Performed with a barbell.
instructions: Sit down and rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms facing DOWN, with the bar held and your wrists just past your knees.
Let your hands drop so the bar lowers toward the floor, feeling a stretch on top of your forearms.
Raise the backs of your hands as high as you can by extending your wrists, keeping your forearms pinned down.
Hold the squeeze at the top for a second.
Lower the bar slowly under control and repeat. Use a light load and a full range — this is a small muscle.

name: Wrist Roller
description: A continuous winding drill that torches the wrist flexors and extensors and builds serious grip endurance. Performed with a wrist roller.
instructions: Hold the roller out in front of you at about shoulder height with both hands, arms straight, and the cord hanging with the weight at the bottom.
Brace your core and keep your arms extended.
Wind the weight up by rolling the bar with one wrist at a time, hand over hand, until the weight reaches the top.
Then reverse the motion and lower the weight slowly with the same continuous wrist action — don't let it drop.
Keep the movement smooth and constant. Your forearms will burn — that's the point.

name: Forearm Pronation
description: A forearm rotation drill working the pronators and supinators that turn the wrist.
instructions: Rest your forearm along your thigh or a bench with your hand off the end, holding the weight so it sits to one side.
Keep your forearm still and your wrist in line with it.
Rotate your forearm to turn your palm up and then down through a full, controlled range.
Pause briefly at each end and feel the muscles that turn the wrist working.
Continue slowly under control and repeat. Move only the forearm — keep the elbow steady.
